record.original_question: For the XXZ spin chain in the critical regime -1 ≤ Δ < 1, study time- and temperature-dependent correlation functions at large separation in space and time, including the correlation function g(n,t) discussed in the paper. Derive an explicit analytic formula for the asymptotic exponential decay of these correlation functions in the joint large-distance, large-time limit.

evidence.quote: Despite these considerable efforts the asymptotics of time and temperature dependent correlation functions, such as g(n, t) (see 13) for the XXZ spin chain, are still out of our reach. We expect that they will decay exponentially like in the previous examples of the isotropic XY spin chain or the δ-function Bose gas but at this moment we do not have such a result.
Open problem: Derive an explicit analytic formula describing the asymptotic exponential decay of time and temperature correlation functions in the critical region (−1 ≤ ∆ < 1) of the XXZ spin chain.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the spin-1/2 XXZ Heisenberg chain on the infinite line with Hamiltonian
  H = J ∑_{n∈ℤ} ( σ^x_n σ^x_{n+1} + σ^y_n σ^y_{n+1} + Δ ( σ^z_n σ^z_{n+1} − 1 ) ),
where σ^{x,y,z}_n are Pauli matrices acting at site n and Δ is the anisotropy parameter, in the critical (massless) regime −1 ≤ Δ < 1. At inverse temperature β > 0 and in thermal equilibrium, define the dynamical two-point correlation function
  g(n,t) = ⟨ σ^-_0(0) σ^+_n(t) ⟩_β = Tr( e^{-β H} σ^-_0 e^{i t H} σ^+_n e^{-i t H} ) / Tr( e^{-β H} ),
together with the analogous longitudinal correlator ⟨ σ^z_0(0) σ^z_n(t) ⟩_β.

Derive an explicit analytic closed-form expression for the leading asymptotic behavior of these correlation functions in the joint limit of large spatial separation n → ∞ and large time t → ∞ (with n/t fixed or in a specified scaling regime). In particular, exhibit the conjectured exponential decay rate as an explicit function of Δ, β, n and t, including the prefactor.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the problem was posed. Dugave, Göhmann, and Kozlowski (2013, arXiv:1305.0118) developed a thermal form factor expansion for the XXZ chain and obtained the large-distance asymptotics of static finite-temperature correlation functions. For the free-fermion XX point, the long-time large-distance asymptotics of dynamical transverse correlators at finite temperature were derived (arXiv:1908.11555, 2020). Subsequent works treat dynamical asymptotics in the massless XXZ regime via thermal form factors, but a fully explicit closed-form formula for the joint large-distance, large-time exponential decay of g(n,t) throughout −1 ≤ Δ < 1 at general temperature is not yet established in complete generality, so the problem remains only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Thermal form factors of the XXZ chain and the large-distance asymptotics of its temperature dependent correlation functions
status_evidence.snippet: Form factors of the quantum transfer matrix of the XXZ chain determine amplitudes in the leading asymptotics of finite-temperature correlation functions.
status_evidence.claim: Static finite-temperature large-distance asymptotics for XXZ have been obtained via thermal form factors.

status_evidence.title: Long-time large-distance asymptotics of the transverse correlation functions of the XX chain in the spacelike regime
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit expression for the leading term in the long-time, large-distance asymptotic expansion of a transverse dynamical two-point function at finite temperature for the XX chain.
status_evidence.claim: Dynamical finite-temperature asymptotics solved at the free-fermion XX point.

status_evidence.title: Multi-point Correlation Functions in the Boundary XXZ Chain at Finite Temperature
status_evidence.snippet: Multi-point correlation functions in the XXZ chain at finite temperature via quantum transfer matrix and thermal form factors.
status_evidence.claim: Framework for dynamical finite-temperature XXZ correlators is being developed but a complete closed-form for all −1≤Δ<1 is not stated.
